headline: Jets place Walker Duehr on waivers
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, the Jets have placed Walker Duehr on waivers. Duehr has yet to play this season due to a lower-body injury.

Since Duehr hasn't played, nothing in the numbers speaks to him directly, but they say a lot about the team around him. Winnipeg is 4-2-2 for 10 points through eight games, yet it has owned only 46.6% of the expected goals so far this season (expected goals measure the quality of chances each side creates, so anything under 50% means the Jets are giving up the better looks). At five-on-five it is 46%, so the lean is not just a special-teams quirk. Goaltending is holding it together: the Jets have saved 3.3 goals more than expected given the shots they have faced, which explains how a team with a below-even chance share sits near the top of its results. Their finishing has slightly lagged, at 0.9 goals fewer than expected. The takeaway is that the record flatters the underlying play, and the roster churn at the margins matters more when the team depends on its goalie to cover for the territorial deficit.
